newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel under pressure from swaps, straight-run.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel under pressure from swaps, straight-run.

text.p: High and low sulphur cracked fuel dropped on Monday as a combination of factors overwhelmed perceptions of tight supply.

Traders said weaker swaps, the continuing threat of Russian straight run finding its way into the cracked market and talk that some outstanding bunker requirement in the Med had been largely met were the main causes for the fall.
But, some dealers felt the tightness was still there and that paper prices were ignoring the wet situation and the Portuguese tender of 150,000 tonnes, which was awarded today.
In the barge market deals were done as low as $109 fob ARA,
down $5 from Friday as sellers competed to shift material.

High sulphur cargoes were also seen weaker. An early October Scandanavian cargo was offered at $108 fob NWE compared with $110 fob NWE before the weekend. One U.K. end user said a straight run cargo was offered at no extra premium to cracked.

Low sulphur cracked was also pulled lower by swaps numbers although requirement was seen into the U.K. and into the Med. A 50kt cargo was sold into Italy on a 50:50 basis, with the fixed price at $125.75 cif. Another cargo was sold ex-Lavera also on 50:50 at $119 fob and high fob +$1.75.
